title: West Side Story
tagline: Two gangs, one table. Nobody rumbles over dessert.
about: On New York's Upper West Side, a former gang member falls for the sister of the rival gang's leader just as the two gangs head for a showdown.
cue: Serve the snacks when the Jets and the Sharks square off across the floor at the dance at the gym.
faces: Upper West Side, Saturday night. All welcome.

    StartersBernardo's tostones with garlic mojoTwice-fried green plantain smashed flat, salted hot, with a sharp garlic, lime and olive oil mojoHow to make it3 green plantains750ml vegetable oil, for frying6 cloves of garlic80ml olive oil2 limes, juiced1 small bunch coriander, chopped1 tsp saltPeel the plantains by slitting the skin lengthways and prising it off, then cut into 3cm pieces.Heat 3cm of the vegetable oil in a heavy pot to 160°C.Fry the plantain in batches until pale gold but still soft inside, then drain.Smash each piece flat to about 1cm with the base of a glass.Crush the garlic to a paste with half the salt, then stir in the olive oil, lime juice and coriander.Turn the oil up to 180°C and fry the smashed plantain again until crisp and golden.Drain on paper towel, sprinkle with the rest of the salt and serve hot with the mojo.Jets' corner cart hot dogs with onion sauceSimmered frankfurts in soft rolls with a sweet, spicy tomato and onion sauce and yellow mustardHow to make it8 frankfurts8 long soft rolls2 brown onions2 tbsp vegetable oil2 tbsp tomato paste1/2 tsp chilli powder1 pinch of ground cinnamon1 tbsp sugar1 tbsp white vinegar125ml water4 tbsp yellow mustardHalve and thinly slice the onions.Cook the onions in the oil over medium heat until soft and pale gold.Stir in the tomato paste, chilli powder, cinnamon, sugar, vinegar and water and simmer until thick and jammy.Simmer the frankfurts in a pot of barely bubbling water until hot through.Warm the rolls in a low oven.Tuck a frankfurt in each roll, spread with mustard and spoon over the onion sauce.Pastelillos de carneAnita's batch, made for the rooftop America.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsMaria's pernil with arroz con gandulesSlow-roasted pork shoulder rubbed with garlic, oregano, cumin and citrus, with sofrito rice, pigeon peas and green olivesHow to make it2kg boneless pork shoulder, skin on10 cloves of garlic2 tbsp dried oregano2 tsp ground cumin1 tbsp sweet paprika1 tbsp salt1 tsp ground black pepper100ml olive oil3 limes, 2 juiced and 1 in wedges1 orange, juiced1 brown onion, finely chopped1 green capsicum, finely chopped1 bunch coriander, stalks chopped, leaves picked2 tbsp tomato paste1/2 tsp ground turmeric2 cups long grain rice400g tin pigeon peas, drained100g green olives750ml vegetable stockBlend the garlic, oregano, cumin, paprika, salt, pepper, 60ml of the olive oil, the lime juice and orange juice to a paste.Score the pork skin, rub the paste all over and into the cuts, cover and marinate in the fridge overnight.Take the pork out of the fridge to come to room temperature and heat the oven to 160°C.Roast skin up for 4 hours, then turn the oven to 230°C for 25 minutes to crackle the skin.While it roasts, soften the onion, capsicum and coriander stalks in the rest of the oil, then stir in the tomato paste, turmeric and rice for 2 minutes.Add the pigeon peas, olives and stock, bring to the boil, cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, then rest 10 minutes off the heat.Rest the pork 15 minutes, pull into chunks with the crackling and serve over the rice with coriander leaves and lime wedges.Officer Krupke's corned beef and cabbageGee, Officer Krupke, the Jets' favourite cop gets his dinnerHow to make it1.5kg corned silverside1 onion, studded with 4 cloves1 tsp black peppercorns2 tbsp brown sugar1 tbsp malt vinegar4 carrots, halved800g potatoes, halved1/2 green cabbage, in wedges40g butter2 tbsp hot English mustardCover the beef with water, add the onion, peppercorns, sugar and vinegar and simmer gently.Add the carrots and potatoes for the last part of cooking.Steam the cabbage wedges until tender and toss with butter.Slice the beef and serve with the vegetables and mustard.SweetsBridal shop coconut flanBaked coconut and vanilla custard set over dark caramel, chilled and turned outHow to make it150g caster sugar3 tbsp water395g tin condensed milk400ml tin coconut milk5 eggs1 tsp vanilla extract1 pinch of saltMelt the sugar with the water over medium heat, without stirring, until deep amber.Pour the caramel into a 20cm round cake tin and swirl to coat the base, then heat the oven to 160°C.Whisk the condensed milk, coconut milk, eggs, vanilla and salt until smooth, then strain into the tin.Sit the tin in a roasting dish and pour in hot water to come halfway up the sides.Bake until just set with a slight wobble in the middle.Lift out of the water and cool on a rack.Chill in the fridge until firm.Run a knife around the edge and turn out onto a plate with a lip to catch the caramel.DrinksDoc's candy store egg creamHomemade chocolate syrup, cold milk and fizzing soda water, stirred hard for a white foam headHow to make it50g cocoa powder150g caster sugar150ml water1 pinch of salt1 tsp vanilla extract500ml very cold full cream milk1 L cold soda waterSimmer the cocoa, sugar, water and salt, stirring, until smooth and glossy, then stir in the vanilla.Cool the chocolate syrup completely.Spoon 2 tbsp syrup into each of 4 tall glasses and add the cold milk.Pour in the soda water in a fast stream while stirring hard with a long spoon until a thick white foam rises.Serve straight away, with the spoon still in.Pineapple tamarind punchGlad Hand's punch.
